prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1434; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of a low-speed head-on collision at a residential intersection. Insured vehicle sustained front-end damage. Claimant reports neck and shoulder discomfort at scene and declined transport by ambulance. Claimant is not represented by counsel. Photos requested from both drivers.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. Claimant describes right shoulder pain radiating into the upper arm, worse with overhead reaching. Claimant has scheduled an evaluation with their primary care provider. Requested medical authorization form and copies of any treatment records. Explained the claims process and that the claimant may take time to seek advice on their own.

Entry 3: Reviewed scene photos and the driver statements. Both parties agree the vehicles were slowing at the time of impact and that airbags did not deploy. Damage estimate for the claimant vehicle received from the appraiser and forwarded to the file. Vehicle inspection set for later this week.

Entry 4: Received preliminary medical report from claimant's provider noting a right rotator cuff strain with limited range of motion. Imaging ordered to rule out tear. Claimant confirmed they have not yet missed work. Reminded claimant that they may consult an attorney at any time and that the company cannot provide legal advice.

Entry 5: Imaging results reviewed. No fracture noted; soft tissue findings consistent with strain. Treatment plan includes physical therapy referral. Sent written update to claimant summarizing open items: repair estimate approval, medical bills submitted to file, and a follow-up call scheduled to check on recovery progress.
